newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy reassures EU on Banco di Napoli.
newsitem.headline: Italy reassures EU on Banco di Napoli.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday that the Italian government had given assurances it would take the necessary measures to enable the EU to clear a capital injection of almost 2.0 trillion lire ($1.3 billion) into Banco di Napoli.

"(Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio) Ciampi has given assurances that the Italian authorities will do whatever is still needed to enable to Commission to clear the recapitalisation of Banco di Napoli," Commission spokesman Willy Helin said.
He was reporting on a telephone conversation between Ciampi and European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert on Thursday.
Van Miert expressed "astonishment" earlier this week about Italy's decision to go ahead with the capital increase of 1.977 trillion lire.
The Commission had indicated in discussions with the Italian government that this should not happen before the conclusion of a procedure to privatise Napoli, Italy's largest southern bank.
The Italian Treasury took temporary control of the bank after it unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995.
The Commission wants to be sure the privatisation operation will ensure the bank's long-term viability before giving its assent to the capital injection, which could amount to state subsidies.

The Commission will also have to review the bids put forward by the potential candidates, especially if they are themselves state controlled, to check that the operation does not involve any more subsidies than planned.
Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) said on Thursday it had decided along with insurer INA to offer to buy 60 percent of Banco di Napoli.
The Italian southern bank plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year and the treasury has given interested parties until December 20 to make offers.
The Treasury said on Tuesday it had kicked off the capital increase for the ailing bank, beginning the underwriting for the operation. $1=1,530
